6.label: Bringing order
6.text: Every strategy takes complexity and gives it structure. The first act of strategic leadership is to bring order to what is chaotic and to name things clearly.

6.label: Value for whom
6.text: An organisation can have alignment, resources, skill and momentum and still fail when its strategy rests on the wrong foundation. A strategy designed mainly to build the reputation of its builders serves the wrong master. Anchor strategy in what the organisation is trying to achieve for its stakeholders. Use this with “creates, delivers and sustains value to its stakeholders”.

8.label: WHY before HOW
8.text: Organisations that rush into execution without clarifying purpose create activity without lasting impact. Strategic clarity emerges when leaders understand why the work exists before deciding how it will be done.

10.label: Naming the gap
10.text: Honestly naming the gap between what has been achieved and what remains is the foundation of the next strategic phase. Organisations that settle for a vague awareness of more to do make little purposeful progress. Name the remaining work specifically, then plan for it.

12.label: Top-down cultures
12.text: When the senior voice ends the conversation, the intelligence that lives at every level of the organisation never reaches the strategy. Use this when participants say their direction was shaped at the top and distributed downward.

12.label: Willing commitment
12.text: Lasting influence grows when people understand the significance of the mission and commit to it voluntarily. Willing commitment produces ownership. Use this with the “aligned or complied?” question.

12.label: Shared understanding
12.text: Intent cannot be executed consistently when people do not know the principles, expectations and boundaries that should govern their decisions.

12.label: Trade-offs
12.text: A strong strategy carries a clear operating logic that guides what is prioritised, how trade-offs are made and how consistency holds under pressure. Execution quality depends on how those decisions are made daily. Use this with “Visible trade-offs”.

13.label: Right destination, right design
13.text: A worthy goal can break down when governance, roles, timing and execution discipline are weak. The right destination still needs the right design. Strategic leadership holds pressure without surrendering clarity. Use this with Process and Thinking Logic.

14.label: Decision Filter
14.text: Organisations without an explicit governing reference point drift into convergent decline: each person makes locally rational decisions that are collectively damaging. Ask participants to name the three governing reference points that override individual preference when they collide. If they cannot name them in plain sentences, the filter is missing.

14.label: Strategic Alignment
14.text: Many legitimate demands fragment attention unless there is a clear organising priority. Effective strategy knows the “one thing” around which competing choices are ordered.

16.label: Partial formation
16.text: The organisations most at risk are often the ones clearly succeeding on one or two dimensions while remaining unformed on the others. What is working reassures them that all is well, so they do not feel the cost of what is missing. Use this to show why all four dimensions matter.

17.label: D1 Customer Only
17.text: Execution can fail from internal dysfunction while external threats are managed well. Sustainable results need attention to both the task and the conditions under which people are expected to perform it.

17.label: D1 Customer Only · signal to watch for
17.text: An organisation declares customer-centricity while its measures and incentives stay internally focused.

17.label: D2 Operations Only
17.text: Cultures calcify when a process or control becomes an end in itself, enforced whether or not it still serves anyone. Ask: “Which rule do your people now serve that no longer benefits them? Fix its purpose or retire it.”

17.label: D3 People Only
17.text: A culture shows in its budget allocations and recognition rituals. Quick audit: list the three things the team invested most resource in last quarter and the three things it most publicly celebrated. If neither list matches the stated values, the values on the wall are decoration.

17.label: D4 Value Only
17.text: Leaders reach for metrics that flatter when they stop trusting the harder, less quantifiable foundations of the work. Ask: “What anxiety is this number meant to soothe?”

17.label: D4 Value Only · enduring value
17.text: Visible momentum does not necessarily indicate sustainable value. Decisions must rest on a clear understanding of what the organisation is trying to build.

19.label: Seeing the larger system
19.text: Good leadership sometimes helps people see a problem within a larger system so that more responsible judgement becomes possible. Use this with “many partial pictures, each accurate and collectively incomplete”.

20.label: An honest baseline
20.text: Strategy begins with an accurate understanding of present reality. Leaders who avoid difficult information protect their comfort at the expense of the institution. Name the true condition without minimising it. Use this before participants score: honest scoring is the point of the assessment.

21.label: Personality-dependent strategy
21.text: A sound strategy is defined clearly enough that a new leader can step in and continue execution. A defined strategic position creates value only when the organisation translates intent into deliberate, consistent action. Use this with the 0–26 band.

21.label: The mission larger than the contributor
21.text: When value becomes inseparable from particular individuals, ego and fragility increase. Strong cultures recognise the contribution while keeping the mission larger than the contributor.

22.label: Present tense of the future
22.text: Teams that can receive a declared outcome and work backward from it to the actions required move from instruction to execution most effectively. Declare the outcome first, then design the process to reach it.

23.label: Silence is a decision
23.text: The leader who is present when a commitment is made and does not challenge it has endorsed it. A plan received without objection binds the organisation to an outcome the leader could have shaped. Use this with “Compete: where trade-off decisions are needed”.

27.label: Strategy carried by people
27.text: What the people who carry a strategy have understood and internalised survives the loss of any document. Build the strategy into their knowledge and conviction. Use this with “Leaders repeat it everywhere”.
